text:
AlertBot: :pager: ALERT — streaming p99 spike detected for model:redwood-4x on eu-west-1. p99 = 2100ms, p95 = 370ms over last 5m. Error rate steady. Auto-escalation -> incidents channel.
Jordan (oncall): seeing the same in dashboards. Spike coincides with last night's int8 calibration rollout (profile: dynamic-fast-int8). Starting triage.
Mike SRE: I can take lead. First guess: int8 calibration fallout on the KV cache path causing dequant stalls on long-context streams.
Anna R: tagging for customer comms. Which tenants hit the SLOs? any paid customers impacted?
Infra Liz: quick check: top affected service routes = /streaming/chat and /streaming/generate. Traffic shifted to int8 nodes ~00:10 UTC. Canary completed last midnight.
Support Sam: Support tickets from 2 customers showing timeouts and aborted streams (EU region). Raising a severity-2.
Jordan (oncall): dump from trace for a slow stream:
```
trace_id=0x7f8e user=acct-cc123 route=/streaming/chat
span decode_kv_cache: 13ms
span dequant_step: 1800ms
span response_streaming: 240ms
```
Mike SRE: dequant_step=1.8s — that matches p99. Looks like dequant hot path regressed after calibration. Could be a fallback in kernel selection hitting an inefficient path.
Anna R: customers notified: "We're investigating increased streaming latency; engineering on it; will update in 20m." (posted to affected tenants)
Infra Liz: quick health commands I ran:
```
redwood infra list-nodes --region=eu-west-1 --model=redwood-4x --precision=int8
# shows 18 nodes, 3 at high CPU, 2 reporting dequant errors
kubectl get pods -n inference | grep redwood-4x
```
Mike SRE: immediate mitigation options:
- rollback precision profile to previous int8-calib-v1
- route streaming traffic to fp16 pool for EU region (fallback)
- throttle new calibration jobs
Which is fastest?
Jordan (oncall): routing to fp16 is lowest-risk and fastest to flip. Start routing for streaming-only routes.
Infra Liz: applied routing change: `route set --region eu-west-1 --model redwood-4x --route /streaming/* -> fp16-pool` (applied at 6076500065)
AlertBot: system note: route update deployed by infra-liz at 6076500065.
Mike SRE: monitoring… p99 dropped from 2100ms -> 480ms within two minutes. p95 back to ~150-200ms. Looks like the fp16 fallback fixes the tail.
Jordan (oncall): good. Next: rollback calibration rollout or patch the calibration routine. We should revert the dynamic-fast-int8 rollout and pause future auto-calibrations.
Mike SRE: starting rollback of precision profile (command):
```
redwood models calibrations rollback --model redwood-4x --to int8-calib-v0 --reason "rollback post-deploy tail spikes"
```
Mike SRE: rollback started at 6076500100. Monitoring kernel selection logs for dequant path.
Infra Liz: paused calibration jobs and revoked the rollout tag on CI at 6076500112.
Support Sam: customers on live calls are seeing improved streams after routing change. One customer reported partial reconnects but no data loss.
Anna R: drafting incident update for product customers: root cause suspected calibration artifact in dynamic quantization path. We'll confirm.
Jordan (oncall): logging follow-ups: collect core dumps, dequant perf counters, and calibration seed used for last rollout. Also flag the canary config that allowed full rollout too quickly.
Mike SRE: quick grep of release notes shows new quant kernel fallback added in 2026-02-28 patch: `kquant-v2`. Might be selecting slower fallback for certain sequence lengths.
Infra Liz: pulled per-node metrics: nodes with high p99 showed elevated L2 cache misses and memcpy spikes during dequant. Suggests an extra reordering step triggered by the new kernel.
Jordan (oncall): action items (short):
- Mike: finish rollback and verify p99 stable (ETA 10m)
- Infra Liz: collect node perf counters and save kernels used (ETA 20m)
- Anna: update customers and internal postmortem stub (ETA 15m)
- Support Sam: correlate support tickets and prepare notes for SEs (ETA 10m)
Mike SRE: rollback completed at 6076500140. p99 now 310-520ms, trending stable. No new timeouts reported.
AlertBot: auto-notify: oncall handoff scheduled — Jordan handing to Mike for next 30m for follow-through.
Jordan (oncall): handing off. Mike will be primary; I'll stay available for comms.
Anna R: posted status update to customers at 6076500155. Message: "We mitigated increased tail latency by routing streaming traffic to fp16 pools and rolling back last int8 calibration. Engineers are collecting artifacts for full RCA."
Support Sam: closing immediate high-touch tickets; leaving follow-ups open.
Mike SRE: follow-up notes: reproduction steps to run in staging:
```
# simulate long-context streaming workload
loadgen --model redwood-4x --precision=int8 --seq-len=2048 --streams=200
# observe dequant timing and kernel selection
trace view --trace-id <id>
```
Infra Liz: saved perf dumps to s3://incidents/6076500000/perf/ and kernels to s3://incidents/6076500000/kernels/ (ids attached)
Jordan (oncall): good work. We avoided customer-facing outage by quick routing and rollback. Next: full postmortem and change to rollout gating (canary duration + perf test). Marking incident as mitigated; keep thread open until RCA.
Mike SRE: noting regression hypothesis: calibration -> selects kquant-v2 path -> triggers tensor-reorder memcpy on large KV entries -> dequant stall for long-context streams. Will validate.
Anna R: I'll schedule a customer-facing summary after the RCA. Thanks team. :heart:
Support Sam: moving internal tickets to incident-6076500000 and tagging SEs.
AlertBot: Incident severity downgraded to S2 at 6076500175. Monitoring continues.
